Appendix

Appendix I — Notation

The mathematical notation in this book follows §2.2 of the revised version of the Agentic Reasoning survey read in Chapter 2. Each chapter keeps the notation of its main paper, and its "Back to the surveys" section gives a table mapping that notation to the symbols below. Section and equation numbers follow the anonymized OpenReview review copy (generated 2026-09-01, 146 pages).

1. Environment and agent — two tuples

The survey writes the environment and the agent separately on purpose. The agent's context is often folded into the environment state, and then, the survey argues, you can no longer see what two agents in the same environment do differently.

Environment — a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP)

E=⟨X,O,A,T,Ω,R,γ⟩

Symbol Meaning Example
X Latent environment state space. The agent cannot observe it All of Wikipedia; the actual state of a file system
O Observation space A user's question, an API response, tool output
A External action space A tool call, the final answer
T Transition kernel (how the state changes) —
Ω Observation kernel (which observation a state yields) —
R Reward Whether the answer is correct, task success
γ∈(0,1) Discount factor —

Agent

G=⟨Z,M,πreason,πexec,U⟩

Symbol Meaning Example
Z Space of reasoning traces. Either a latent plan or a thought written out in words (chain-of-thought) ReAct's Thought, the intermediate steps of CoT
M The agent's internal memory and context space MemGPT's main context, Reflexion's store of reflections
πreason Reasoning policy — produces a reasoning trace zt from the history —
πexec Execution policy — produces an external action at from the history and the reasoning trace —
U System-update operator (Eq. 5) Reflexion accumulating reflections, Voyager adding skills

Z and M are design choices of the agent. The environment neither observes them nor is changed by them. Two agents that differ in Z or M face the same E.

2. Symbols at time t

Symbol Meaning
ot∈O Observation at time t
zt∈Z Reasoning trace (thought) at time t
at∈A External action at time t
ht=(o≤t,z<t,a<t) History. After seeing ot the agent produces zt, then at
mt∈M Internal memory state summarizing the history
rt Reward at time t
τ=(h0,z0,a0,h1,z1,a1,…) Trajectory
θ Model parameters (weights)

Policy factorization (Eq. 1)

πθ(zt,at∣ht)=πreason(zt∣ht)⏟internal thought·πexec(at∣ht,zt)⏟external action

The survey notes that Eq. 1 is only an application of the chain rule and has no content by itself. It holds for any joint distribution of (zt,at). The content lies in the three assumptions posited alongside it.

Objective

J(θ)=𝔼τ[∑t≥0γtrt]

3. The three assumptions A0, A1 and A2

Assumption Statement Who posits it Where this book meets it
A0 Ordering and externality zt is generated before at and is not emitted to the environment. T and Ω are "functions of at alone" (the survey's wording; see the note below the table for how to read it) Every system the survey covers The line between a single forward pass and agentic reasoning. Chapter 4 and Chapter 6
A1 Memory sufficiency πreason(zt∣ht)=πreason(zt∣mt) — mt is a sufficient statistic for ht An assumption made by systems, not a property of the setting Chapter 12. Failures on long-horizon tasks are failures of A1 (survey §4.2)
A2 Execution sufficiency πexec(at∣ht,zt)=πexec(at∣zt) Not assumed in general. It holds for plan-then-execute architectures and fails for interleaved architectures such as ReAct Chapter 6 (where ReAct breaks it), Chapter 15 (the channel that carries an observation straight into an action)

How to read "functions of at alone" in A0. In section 1, T and Ω are kernels on the latent state X, so the next state and observation also depend on the current environment state. This book reads the survey's shorthand as a statement of blocking: the only thing the agent passes to the environment is at. The exact form that writes the kernel out with the state (for example T(xt+1∣xt,at)) is not in the survey, and this reading is the editor's. The point is that zt and mt do not enter the kernels as arguments.

4. Three optimization targets — what gets changed

The revised survey classifies agentic reasoning techniques by what they optimize. The two modes of the pre-review manuscript (in-context and post-training) became three in the revised version.

Mode What it changes What it holds fixed Time scale Examples in this book
In-context reasoning (inference-time search) The reasoning trace z — searches over Z to raise a heuristic value v^(ht,z) θ Within one episode CoT (Chapter 4), ToT (Chapter 5), ReAct (Chapter 6). The RAG of Chapter 8 (Lewis et al. 2020) fine-tunes its query encoder and generator, so it belongs on the θ side; the survey cites it only as a reference point for the three regimes
System-level optimization (self-evolution) The system state S — memory, tool library, code (Eq. 5) θ Across episodes k=1,…,K Reflexion (Chapter 11, Verbal Evolution), Voyager (Chapter 12 and Chapter 20, Procedural Evolution), MemGPT's external memory (Chapter 12)
Post-training (policy optimization) The parameters θ — updates the policy toward long-horizon reward rt — Training stage Toolformer (Chapter 7), Self-RAG (Chapter 10), InstructGPT (Chapter 16), DeepSeek-R1 (side paper of Chapter 4)

System update (Eq. 5)

Sk+1←U(Sk,τk,Fk)

Sk is the evolvable system state at episode k (explicit memory, tool library, code), τk is that episode's trajectory, and Fk is environment feedback (rewards, execution errors). The survey divides self-evolution into three by the kind of S: Verbal Evolution (S is written reflections and guidelines — Reflexion), Procedural Evolution (S is executable tools and skills — Voyager) and Structural Evolution (S is the agent's code or architecture itself — AlphaEvolve).

The three search objectives of in-context reasoning. ReAct is greedy decoding that alternates thoughts z and actions a. For methods that treat fragments of thought as nodes, the survey does not lump everything into one objective but writes three. ToT expands a frontier under a node budget B, keeps only children with value v^ϕ(u)≥κ, and picks the highest-scoring leaf of depth at most H (argmaxu∈LHv^ϕ(u)); MCTS uses an upper-confidence rule on the backed-up value Q(u,u′)=W(u,u′)/N(u,u′) from rollouts; and process rewards and step-level verifiers use a path sum (Eq. 2).

τ⋆∈argmaxτ∈ΓH∑tv^ϕ(ut)(Eq. 2)

Here ΓH is the set of feasible trajectories of depth at most H (a different symbol from the transition kernel T), and v^ϕ is a step-level verifier or process reward model. The survey notes that the restriction to ΓH is what makes the maximization well defined.

Representative equations of post-training. PPO is the standard, and GRPO is widely used for reasoning tasks (Eqs. 3 and 4). GRPO normalizes the rewards of G outputs for the same prompt q within the group to form the advantage A^i=(ri−μ)/(σ+δ), and does away with the value network. This book does not treat post-training in depth, so for Eqs. 3 and 4 see §2.2 of the survey.

5. Multiple agents

Symbol Meaning
N Number of agents
πi Policy of agent i. The joint policy π is the composition of the πi
C Communication channel
oti Observation of agent i. It includes the messages ct−1−i its peers sent at the previous step

The survey writes this as a decentralized partially observable setting (Dec-POMDP), and gives the fact that one agent's external action becomes a prompt that triggers another agent's internal reasoning as the difference between communication and mere signal transmission. Used in Chapter 13.

Chapter 16 InstructGPT Reward model loss −1(K2)𝔼(x,yw,yl)~D[logσ(rθ(x,yw)−rθ(x,yl))] (Eq. 1 of the paper) θ mode. Reading it as a paired-comparison model is the editor's bridge
Chapter 17 Evaluation pass@k =1−(1−p)k, pass^k =pk (when trials are independent) Evaluation metrics. They correspond to estimating R
Chapter 18 Statistics Standard error, clustered standard error, paired comparison, power Uncertainty of evaluation results

7. Conventions

  • Sets are capitals (Z, M); elements are lowercase with subscripts (zt, mt).
  • The survey's πreason and πexec are used as they are.
  • Probability is p(·), expectation 𝔼[·], set size |·|.

4. Names that overlap

"CRAG" is also used for a RAG benchmark, CRAG – Comprehensive RAG Benchmark (Xiao Yang et al., arXiv 2406.04744, NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks). The CRAG of this book is Corrective RAG (L09). A search for "harness survey" also turns up From Question Answering to Task Completion: A Survey on Agent System and Harness Design (Jianyuan Guo et al., arXiv 2606.20683). This book's L01 is not that paper but "Agent Harness Engineering: A Survey" by Junjie Li et al.

5. What could not be settled

Item What remains unconfirmed
L22 Agentic Reasoning survey Whether the section and table numbers of the official TMLR version (camera-ready) match the anonymized review copy. As of 2026-10-05 the OpenReview record is still the anonymized review copy and the paper is not on the TMLR list on jmlr.org, so there is no version to compare against. arXiv has no v3, and v2 has the same body as v1. To be compared again when the camera-ready appears
L18 MemGPT Whether it was published at a conference. On 2026-10-05 the OpenReview records of ICLR 2024 and 2025 and NeurIPS 2023 and 2024 (including public records of rejected and withdrawn submissions), the arXiv metadata and OpenAlex were searched, and no publication record was found, so it is listed as a preprint. A submission withdrawn privately cannot be checked

Appendix IV — Video List

This appendix gathers the lists from each chapter's "Videos" section in chapter order. There are three labels. [Author] marks a talk by an author of the paper or from an official channel, [Review] a paper review by a research lab or study group, and [Secondary] a third party's summary, a talk on the same theme, or a summary that appears to be automatically generated. Watch [Secondary] videos alongside the original. The title and channel of every video were checked through YouTube oEmbed. The 57 links checked on October 4, 2026 were queried again on October 5, 2026, and all their titles matched; the 11 added that day were checked the same day (68 in all). The check covers titles and channels only; the editor did not watch the videos themselves. Videos may disappear or change address.

Videos in Korean are kept and marked (in Korean). As in each chapter, titles and channel names in Korean are given in English, translated or romanized by the editor.

How this book was made

The editor made this book with Claude Code. Because it is text produced with generative AI, errors may remain even after it was checked against the originals. The chapter plan, the bibliographic checks, the chapter drafts and the checks against the originals were done in the following order.

  1. The list of papers first proposed in the study group was checked bibliographically. Titles, authors and submission dates were checked against arXiv metadata, and venues against official conference listings (NeurIPS and ICLR proceedings, the ACL Anthology, the TMLR listing, Crossref DOIs). Seven entries on the list with the wrong year, venue or title were corrected (Appendix III).
  2. The order of the twenty chapters and the reading range of each were set: one question each chapter answers, the sections and figures to read in 50 minutes, and the papers to send to the side-paper notes.
  3. A draft was written for each chapter. Factual claims (section, figure and table numbers, numbers, quotations) were written only if they had been confirmed in the original PDF. Sentences inside figures were read by rendering the PDF.
  4. Each chapter was checked independently. A process separate from the one that wrote the draft received only the draft and the originals, compared them sentence by sentence, and fixed what was wrong. The numbers in the statistical reanalyses were recalculated during the check.
  5. All the chapters were bound into one file to make the screen edition (HTML) and the print edition (PDF), and every link was counted to confirm that it works.

The Agentic Reasoning survey was read in the revised TMLR version on OpenReview (an anonymized review copy, generated 2026-09-01). The version on arXiv differs from the revised version in its section and table numbers and in its categories. Once the formal TMLR version is out, the numbers will need to be checked again.

How this English edition was made

This English edition was translated from Korean edition 1.0 (October 5, 2026) by the editor working with Claude Code. Quotations that were originally in English were restored from the original papers, posts and specifications rather than translated back from Korean; where a passage could not be found in the original, the quotation marks were removed and the passage was rendered in indirect speech. Tables reproduced from the originals were returned to the original English labels. Korean-language sources, including Korean-language videos and blog posts, are kept and marked "(in Korean)"; their titles and channel names are given in English, translated or romanized by the editor. Numbers were carried over from the Korean edition and checked against it; where the Korean edition was found to be wrong, as with the count of videos (67, not 56), this edition follows the originals. Their notation changed only where English needs it (for example, Korean counting units written as thousands or millions). The labels in the diagrams were translated; their shapes and positions were not changed. Where the Korean edition counts meetings, this edition counts chapters (Chapter 0 to Chapter 20). Before publication, an AI model from a different company (OpenAI Codex), given only the Korean and English texts and the sources they cite, compared the two editions sentence by sentence; each of its findings was rechecked against the originals and either fixed or answered with a written reason for leaving it.

When you use this book

  • It does not replace the originals. This book is a guide to reading the originals, and presentations are made from the originals. When you carry numbers onto presentation slides, look at the original table again, not this book.
  • When the numbers date from. The performance numbers in the papers come from the models of their time (PaLM-540B, GPT-3, GPT-4 and so on). Do not use them to compare with today's models.
  • Peer review. Several of the 2026 sources are preprints. The Harness survey is posted on OpenReview but has not gone through conference or journal review. Do not cite their claims and numbers as settled results.
  • Company documents. The posts by Anthropic, OpenAI, Manus and Chroma are prescriptions drawn from building their own products. Read them as design guidance, not as generalized empirical evidence.
  • The "Rereading with a statistician's eye" sections are reanalyses done outside the papers. The editor calculated them using only the numbers printed in the papers, and they are not meant to overturn the papers' conclusions. The "bridge" analogies were laid down by the editor and are kept apart from the papers' claims.
  • Distribution and copyright. Do not redistribute paper PDFs; share links (arXiv, OpenReview, conference pages). Under its terms, the GAIA data may not be reshared outside its gated repository or published in a crawlable form.
  • Security exercises. Do prompt-injection exercises only in an environment you own or in a public evaluation environment (AgentDojo and the like).
  • Links. All links were checked on October 4, 2026. Blogs and videos may disappear or change address.
  • Errors and revisions. This book will keep being revised. If you find a statement that differs from its source, please report it through the issue tracker (Issues) of the public repository or to the editor. Corrections will be made in a new edition with a new date.
  • A personal study resource. The editor compiled this book as part of personal study. It is unrelated to the views or work of any institution the editor belongs to.
